findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion in test_review_bot.py that a finding carrying a `standing` object produces the literal 'since patchset <N>' in the composed Gerrit text AFTER passing through `_translate_findings`, so AC9 exercises the adapter allowlist end-to-end rather than only grepping source.
evidence: Plan: "`grep -c \"since patchset\" src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` ... return >= 1; `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q`"
Scope: "`review_bot/adapter.py` (`_translate_findings` `:122` drops keys outside the allowlist — carry `standing`)"
Verify taxonomy (1)/(4): a source grep is a substring/fixture-validity false-positive — it proves presence in source, not that the path fires with real carried data through adapter->publish.
findings.finding: AC9's proving commands (grep 'since patchset' in finding_publish.py source + a bare `pytest test_review_bot.py -q`) confirm the render string EXISTS in source but do not prove a carried `standing` finding actually survives the adapter's `_translate_findings` allowlist extension and renders 'since patchset N' end-to-end. Since adapter.py:122 drops keys outside the allowlist, the whole feature silently no-ops if the allowlist edit regresses, yet the grep still passes.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, line 'Gerrit marks carried findings and the prompt names them'
scenarios: A future refactor tightens the adapter allowlist and drops `standing`; the grep still matches the format string, so CI stays green while Gerrit never marks any carried finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the bare pytest line with a targeted node id and assert on the rendered output, e.g. `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k standing_since_patchset -q` where that test feeds a standing finding through adapter._translate_findings into finding_publish and asserts `"since patchset 2"` appears in the emitted comment body.

evidence: Plan: 'standing wording is appended code-review-locally in code_review_verify_inputs and in code-review-verify.md; verify.py changes only prior_findings_block's ... docstring'
verify.py:101-108 finding_listing renders '### finding index {i}\nclaim/criteria/evidence/impact' only — no standing/origin field
code_review_verify_inputs (workflow_ops.py:270-275) builds instructions via review_kernel.verify_instructions(list(enumerate(findings))) — the kernel listing, unchanged by this plan
grep confirms code-review-verify.md currently has no 'standing' text, so the appended prose is the only place the category is named
Plan: 'finders never see them' and the standing object is not part of the listing, so the verifier has no per-item signal to match the instruction against
findings.finding: The plan appends 'standing finding' / 'carried from an earlier patchset' instruction wording to the Pass-2 verifier prompt, but the per-finding listing the verifier reads (shared-kernel finding_listing, which the plan deliberately leaves unchanged) renders only claim/criteria/evidence/impact with NO per-finding standing marker — so the verifier cannot tell which listed finding the standing instruction applies to (instruction-locality / pink-elephant: an instruction naming a category with no locatable referent).
findings.location: Approach > 'Shared kernel: no behaviour change'; Scope (code-review-verify.md); AC 'Gerrit marks carried findings and the prompt names them'
scenarios: Pass-2 verifies a batch containing one injected standing finding plus fresh findings; the prompt's 'standing findings' clause has no per-finding anchor, so the verifier either ignores it or misapplies it to fresh findings
findings.suggested_fix: In code_review_verify_inputs, after the kernel finding_listing, append a per-index note enumerating which indices are standing (with origin patchset) — WITHOUT exposing standing.origin_decision (preserving independence) — and word the code-review-verify.md clause to reference that note.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State (and pin in a test) that the injected `standing` object survives Pass-2 verify and Pass-3 `code_review_decide` onto the emitted surfaced finding, so next-run `standing_items()` can classify an already-carried item `withdrawn` (the one-shot bound).
evidence: Plan: '`withdrawn` — the item ITSELF carries a `standing` object: already carried once. NOT carried.'
Plan: 'an item is carried AT MOST ONCE, so the chain ends after one patchset.'
sidecar.py:83 `_with_norm_ids` preserves keys via `{**f, "norm_id": ...}` (so PERSISTENCE at emit is fine) — but the gap is upstream, at verify/decide, which the plan does not address
code_review_decide (workflow_ops.py:447-460) re-buckets finding dicts; the plan asserts it READS standing.origin_decision but not that it PRESERVES the standing object on the surfaced finding
findings.finding: The 'withdrawn' one-shot anti-ratchet depends on the injected `standing` object being PRESERVED through Pass-2 verify and Pass-3 decide onto the emitted surfaced finding, but the plan only shows it persists at build_payload; it never establishes that code_review_decide/pass3_over_findings carry the `standing` key forward. If decide reconstructs finding dicts and drops unknown keys, standing_items() can never see 'the item ITSELF carries a standing object', the carry stops being one-shot, and an UNCHANGED region replays forever — the permanent ratchet (deceitful-flannel-jerboa) the plan claims to prevent.
findings.location: Approach → 'State — one rule per value' (`withdrawn`) and 'Termination (anti-ratchet)'; Scope edit to workflow_ops.py `code_review_decide`
scenarios: PS2 raises a finding at a.py:40; PS3 leaves a.py byte-identical and carries it (still-present); PS4 also leaves a.py untouched — if `standing` did not survive decide on PS3's emit, standing_items() on PS4 cannot classify it `withdrawn` and re-carries it, and so on for every later untouched patchset
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit invariant that code_review_decide preserves the `standing` object on every decided finding it emits (it already reads `standing.origin_decision`), and add an AC/test asserting a carried finding's persisted surfaced payload retains `standing.state` so a second carry classifies `withdrawn`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document how a REGION_UNKNOWN-because-DELETED cited file is treated by `still-present` — either classify a deleted cited path as `addressed`/not-carried, or state why re-injecting a dangling citation is acceptable.
evidence: Plan: 'still-present — ... or the signal is unresolvable (REGION_UNKNOWN: multi-file, absent path, error). CARRIED'
region_gate.py:66-67: 'if current == attest._ABSENT_HASH or prior == attest._ABSENT_HASH: return REGION_UNKNOWN' — a deletion classifies UNKNOWN, which the plan carries
Plan's grounded-only guard requires non-empty evidence but does not require the cited path to still exist
findings.finding: `still-present` folds REGION_UNKNOWN into 'carried', and region_for_finding returns REGION_UNKNOWN when the cited file was DELETED (`_ABSENT_HASH` on either side). Carrying such an item re-injects a finding whose `location` points at a path that no longer exists, handing the Pass-2 verifier a citation it cannot ground.
scenarios: PS2 raises a finding at a.py:40; PS3 DELETES a.py and does not re-emit the finding → region UNKNOWN → carried as still-present, injecting a finding citing a deleted file into PS3's Pass-2
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the `_ABSENT_HASH` (deleted cited file) sub-case of REGION_UNKNOWN as `addressed` (not carried) rather than still-present, since a deletion is affirmative evidence the region was acted on — mirroring the REGION_CHANGED rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the leaf with the parent's 'applies to every child' guard-test rule: either add an AC pinning a construct-uniqueness guard for the carry-forward mechanism (one implementation under src/rebar), or record in the leaf that, as a hardening child adding new behaviour, the construct-uniqueness guard is inapplicable and the parent's 'own recorded criteria' carve-out governs.
evidence: Parent Approach: 'Each child ... lands with a construct-uniqueness guard that asserts on the construct's distinctive atoms', and the 'Guard-test construction rule' header says '(applies to every child)'.

Parent AC explicitly names `nitro-zombie-mealworm` among the HARDENING children that 'deliberately ADD behaviour and lines, so the two consolidation guarantees do not apply to them and they are governed by their own recorded criteria' — this carve-out names only the no-behaviour-change and net-negative guarantees, not the guard-test rule.
Leaf ACs assert '— no second mechanism' and 'The shared kernel is untouched beyond a docstring' but include no construct-uniqueness guard test.

The guard is a consolidation device (one implementation per collapsed construct); a hardening child adds new behaviour with no duplicated computation to collapse, so its applicability here is genuinely ambiguous — hence coached, not blocking.
findings.finding: The parent epic's Approach states a 'Guard-test construction rule (applies to every child)' requiring each child to land a construct-uniqueness guard, but the leaf's Scope and Acceptance Criteria specify no construct-uniqueness guard — they assert single-mechanism intent ('no second mechanism', 'the shared kernel is untouched beyond a docstring') without a guard test that pins that only one carry-forward implementation exists under src/rebar.
findings.location: Leaf Scope / Acceptance Criteria vs parent 2ddd 'Guard-test construction rule (applies to every child; approved 2026-08-21)'
scenarios: A future patch adds a second, divergent carry-forward path (e.g. re-emitting inside the workflow rather than via standing_items) and nothing fails, silently recreating the multi-copy defect class the epic exists to prevent.
